thread:
maria: Heads up — we just started getting p99 latency regressions after the v8 rollout. Spike started at ~12:28 UTC and lines up with a big shift in subtoken density on a handful of hosts (gpu-14, gpu-21). :eyes:

jamie: On it. Initial profiler shows a kernel handoff around step ~512 where execution falls back from optimized attention kernel to the generic path. Perf counters show a KV cache hit-rate drop at same time.

tariq: Dumping batch/seqlen distribution now. Asking autoscaler if noisy neighbor scheduling changed.

perf-bot: ALERT p99_latency > 300ms for route:/v1/generate on cluster:us-west-2 between 12:28-12:34 UTC.

maria: Linking profiler trace: https://perfci.internal/reports/2005001234/v8-rollout-trace (private). Look at kernel_select reasons and input shapes column.

jamie: Quick snapshot from profiler (excerpt):
```
kernel: flash_attn_fast -> fallback_block
input_seq_len: 512
batch_size: 1-3 (many singletons)
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.72 -> 0.45
kernel_select_reason: seqlen_threshold + subtoken_fragmentation
```

andrew: This smells like tokenizer change increasing subtoken count for common prompts, pushing more requests past our fast-path seqlen threshold. Batcher heuristics then create very small batches with long seqs — bad combo.

tariq: Batch histogram (last 10m): [1: 62%, 2: 18%, 3-8: 15%, >8: 5%] — huge singleton tail. Seqlen median jumped from 220->410 post-rollout.

maria: So two things: (1) kernel chooses fallback when seqlen>384, (2) batcher prefers low-latency single-request dispatch for these routes, causing small batches and underutilized GPU kernels. Also KV cache miss rate rises because subtokenization changes cause fewer prefix reuses.

jamie: Hypothesis: tokenizer v8 introduced extra prefix tokens for system prompts, shifting distribution. Reverting tokenizer to v7 for a small canary would be the fastest verification.

andrew: Quick mitigations I can push: bump batcher aggregation window by 20ms for routes impacted, and relax seqlen threshold to consider alternative optimized kernels (if safe). I have a patch ready for batcher: PR #4521.

tariq: Scoped canary for tokenizer revert on 5% of traffic? ops wants to avoid rollback across entire fleet w/o more evidence.

maria: Do the canary and the batcher bump in parallel on a small hostset. If p99 drops, great. If not, we need kernel-side fallback tuning.

deploy-bot: Started canary: tokenizer:v7 on hostset:canary-gpu (5% traffic) — rollout 12:42 UTC.

perf-bot: Notice: p99 on canary hosts dropped from 430ms -> 210ms within 2 minutes of canary.

andrew: Pushing batcher aggregation +20ms to canary now.

jamie: After both changes: overall cluster p99 down ~55%, KV hit-rate on canary recovered to 0.88, host-local GPU utilization improved.

maria: Great. Next steps: 1) Roll tokenizer:v7 back to full while we hotfix tokenizer v8 tokenization rules (reduce prefix insertion). 2) Improve batcher heuristics: add adaptive aggregation that considers recent seqlen histogram. 3) Add a kernel_select telemetry tag for tokenizer-version so we can correlate in future.

tariq: I'll file the postmortem and include the profiler traces + batch histograms. Also adding an alert for sudden subtoken-density drift.

maria: Thanks everyone. We'll track follow-ups in the rollout issue and schedule a short retro tomorrow. :thumbsup:
